This misreading of the evidence together with the opinion of the doctor in the report of the first post-mortem examination pervaded the mind of the learned trial judge and consequently he jumped to the conclusion that it was not a case of homicidal death in view of his presumption that Monowara committed suicide by hanging. 

 27. Earliest information about the cause of death is to be found from the deposition of Doctor Feroz and the two nurses of the Holy Family Hospital who, we have said already, are truthful witnesses. They deposed that the persons who brought Monowara to the hospital insisted on stomach-wash stating that she had taken much Seduxen tablets. This statement is admissible in evidence as res gestae. Sections 6 and 7 of the Evidence Act allow it as an exception to hearsay rule obviously due to its spontaneity as well as immediacy to the occurrence. So we can start with the investigation of the cause of Monowara's death with the presumption that she took much Seduxen. 

 "113A. Presumption as the abetment of suicide by .a married woman. When the suicide by a woman had been abetted by her husband or any relative of her husband and it is shown that she had committed suicide within a period of seven years from the date of her marriage and that her husband or such relative of her husband had subjected her to cruelty, the court may presume, having regard to all the other circumstances of the case, that such suicide had been abetted by her husband or by such relative of her husband.
